newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes, workers agree cost cuts in Bremen.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes, workers agree cost cuts in Bremen.

text.p: German car maker Mercedes-Benz AG said on Friday it reached an agreement with workers to reduce labour costs enough to keep its Bremen plant operating beyond the year 2000.

After three months of negotiations, workers and plant managers agreed to extend the plant's production week to 105 hours, beginning in 1999. Workers also accepted cuts in paid work breaks and agreed to take time off as compensation for some overtime hours.
In exchange, plant management called off a plan to close the facility in 2000, and said it would continue hiring apprentices through the turn of the century, Mecedes said.
In 1996 the plant employed 13,500 workers, including 132 apprentices, and produced 240,000 C-Class and Roadster SL and SLK cars.
